news.title: Manchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offer
news.lede: Real Madrid interested after World Cup performance. Midfielder’s contract at City expires in June 2027. Manchester City are hopeful that Rodri will sign a new contract, but the club are braced for a bid from Real Madrid for the midfielder as well as moves from other suitors. Rodri’s contract expires in June next year and he has failed to sign City’s new deal, which has been on the table for a while.

news.title: Infantino after the 2026 World Cup: “You sow hatred, we unite the world”
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino took to social media to have his say on the World Cup and get more than one thing off his chest: "To all those who missed our beautiful sport, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the tears, the deception and the joy. To all of you who missed the chance to see children, newborn babies, grandparents and parents coming together for this wonderful event, I apologise because the matches are over and I am sorry you missed all that joy and togetherness - the FIFA president's message reads -. I am sorry you were so overwhelmed by hate and criticism that you missed everything. To those who, behind their pens and papers, behind their screens, spread hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting in the second row, we at FIFA are on the front line organising, working hard and putting on the greatest show in the world.

news.title: Dani Olmo rejects Argentina assistant’s apology as he accuses him of lying about punch
news.lede: Olmo was struck by Roberto Ayala in what was one of several flashpoints during the ugly post-match scenes that marred the contest. Ayala later attempted to downplay the incident with Olmo, claiming it was 'more of a shove' and that he'd 'obviously' apologise to the Spaniard if they met in person. But Olmo, speaking to Spanish newspaper Diari de Terrassa, came back swinging. "Someone who says they're sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, is surely not sorry," Olmo said.

news.title: Main player in World Cup final suddenly ends his career with immediate effect
news.lede: Slavko Vincic has brought his career to an end. The Slovenian referee, who took charge of the World Cup final, has officiated his last match in professional football, the Slovenian Football Association report. Vincic has decided to stop refereeing at the age of 46. After taking charge of the World Cup final, he feels he has achieved everything.

news.title: 'Sorry you were so consumed by hate!' - Gianni Infantino blasts FIFA critics after 'most outstanding' World Cup
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has hit back at his detractors in extraordinary fashion, claiming that those who criticised the 2026 World Cup were "consumed by hate." In a lengthy and defiant statement, the head of world football’s governing body defended the tournament’s legacy and urged his opponents to "meditate or pray" instead of spreading negativity. In the wake of a tournament that was as much defined by its off-field drama as its on-field heroics, Infantino has chosen to go on the offensive. The FIFA president used his personal Instagram and the organisation’s official channels to deliver a stinging rebuke to the journalists and critics who questioned the logistics and integrity of the 2026 World Cup across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

news.title: 'It will continue to hurt': Kylian Mbappe breaks silence after France's World Cup heartbreak
news.lede: France captain Kylian Mbappe has shared an emotional message with supporters following Les Bleus' disappointing end to their FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign, admitting that the pain of missing out on the trophy will stay with him despite his historic individual achievements.France's title bid ended with a 2-0 semifinal defeat to Spain, before they were beaten 6-4 by England in the third-place playoff. Mbappe finished the tournament as the Golden Boot winner with 10 goals and became the highest goalscorer in FIFA World Cup history with 22 goals, overtaking Lionel Messi's tally. However, the striker said team success was always the priority.' It will continue to hurt'In a heartfelt letter published in the French regional press, Mbappe admitted that the disappointment of not lifting the World Cup remains difficult to accept."

news.title: World Cup final referee retires just one week after controversial clash as statement is issued
news.lede: The Slovenian official oversaw the ill-tempered clash at the MetLife Stadium, which saw Spain clinch their second world title with a 1-0 win over Argentina after extra time. But Vincic's performance came in for criticism, as he allowed the 2022 champions' physical approach to continue throughout the game. Enzo Fernandez was sent off towards the end of normal time for a second yellow card, before the final descended into chaos at full time. A mass brawl broke out when Argentina's players were involved in a series of bust-ups after the final whistle.

news.title: Infantino Defends FIFA With Claim Over Iran’s World Cup Entry
news.lede: WANA (Jul 27) – Gianni Infantino, president of FIFA, defended the organization’s handling of the 2026 World Cup in an open letter, accusing critics of spreading false narratives and “hate speech.” He also said that Iran’s national team entered the United States without problems, a statement that has drawn attention to previous concerns over the visa process and the challenges surrounding Iran’s participation in the tournament. In his letter, Infantino stressed that the 2026 World Cup was held in a secure environment and argued that football can play a role beyond political disputes. Referring to the participation of teams from countries facing political crises, he said members of Iran’s national team had received visas and were able to take part in the competition.
